title: Region affinity negotiator with hosted evacuation safeguards and variant demotion ladder
creator: Asha Mukherjee
description: Design and implement a 'region affinity negotiator': a routing layer component that enforces tenant-level region affinity for Dedicated capacity while coordinating graceful evacuation to Hosted when Dedicated capacity is constrained. The negotiator should respect per-tenant reservations, latency-SLOs, and model-variant compatibility, and apply a deterministic 'variant demotion ladder' to pick fallback models. Primary goals: preserve Dedicated guarantees for high-priority tenants, avoid cascading cold-starts in Hosted, and provide transparent telemetry for cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator enforces tenant region affinity and respects soft-reserve reservations (soft-reserve tokens) for P0/P1 tenants
When Dedicated capacity is unavailable, negotiator uses a hysteresis window to trigger hosted evacuation rather than immediate failover
Variant demotion ladder selects a compatible fallback model and applies quantization/latency-aware scoring to pick the target hosted variant
Circuit-breaker prevents >20% of requests for any tenant from spilling over to hosted for more than 2 minutes without escalation
New routing decisions are recorded in request traces and console dashboards with per-tenant cost delta and latency impact
Runbook entry exists describing steps for manual override, tenant preemption, and rollback
tasks: Spec: finalize negotiation state machine and signals (capacity, queue depth, p99 latency, KV hit rate)
Prototype: implement negotiator middleware in staging with feature flag
Model compatibility service: extend model catalog API to expose fallback compatibility matrix
Policy engine: implement hysteresis + soft-reserve token accounting + circuit-breaker rules
Telemetry: add cost/latency breakdown and per-tenant spillover counters to console
E2E tests: simulate dedicated eviction, hosted cold-starts, and tenant preemption scenarios
Runbook & playbook: draft and review with SRE and Support
comments: 2026-02-25 — Asha: Initial spec drafted. Focused on making soft-reserve non-blocking so we don't starve hosted for background workloads.
2026-02-28 — Liam: Reviewed state machine; requested clearer signal ordering when both latency and capacity alarms fire simultaneously. Also proposed a 90s hysteresis window to reduce flip-flop.

2026-03-02 — PM (Ravi Patel): Important to expose per-tenant cost delta in console so customers understand hosted spillover billing. Add a 'customer-visible explanation' header in responses when spillover occurs.
2026-03-05 — Design (Maya Chen): UX note — show spilled requests in tenant timeline view and provide rollback toggle for admins; avoid exposing internal model names to customers.

2026-03-08 — SRE (Ibrahim K.): Running chaos test on staging. Observed a thundering herd on hosted variants when eviction policy demoted to smallest-latency variant. Need backoff + jitter in negotiator.
2026-03-10 — Liam: Implemented token-bucket backoff and jitter; updated proto to include 'spill_reason' enum. Added small internal flag to limit initial spill rate to 5% per-tenant for 30s.
2026-03-12 — Asha: Integrating model-compatibility matrix from mgmt service. Next: load-test fine-grained token accounting against multi-tenant trace replay.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: aggressive immediate evacuation minimizes latency SLO misses for individual requests but risks high Hosted cost and cold-start spikes; hysteresis + soft-reserve aims to balance these.
Variant demotion ladder: primary -> quantized-primary -> faster-small -> hosted-compat-v1. Ladder chosen by (compatibility, p95 latency delta, token-cost ratio).
Soft-reserve tokens: allocated per-tenant and decayed over time; tokens do not block routing but influence score to prefer Dedicated unless depletion threshold hit.

Circuit-breaker policy: per-tenant and per-region. Trips when sustained spillover rate >20% for sliding 2-minute window; on trip, negotiator stalls further spillover and escalates to ops and automated throttles.
Observability: trace payload will include negotiated path (dedicated|hosted), chosen_variant, reason_code, cost_estimate_usd, and latency_estimate_ms.
Rollout plan: staged feature-flag rollout to 5 pilot tenants (low-risk), broadening to 20 tenants after 2 weeks of stable SPILL rates <0.5% and no console alerts.
Incident ref: lessons from INC-2026-03-02-dedicated-evacuate — root cause was synchronous demotion across tenants causing hosted cold-start cascade. Negotiator design intentionally staggers demotion.
Open questions: how to surface fallback model fingerprint in audit logs without leaking model internals; whether to allow tenant-configurable spill thresholds (opt-ins).
